source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade and Downgrade FPGA firmware by Redfish when system is booted
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + FPGA image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- FPGA downgrade via Redfish (system is booted): the agent needs the exact user-provided FPGA image first the SUT must be booted first and the host OS running for the flash, then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the FPGA version changed, only one BMC reset happened, and the SUT still boots/passes self-checks.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: FPGA firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

original_test_intent: Exercise approved FPGA firmware upgrade and downgrade through Redfish while the host is booted, and prove successful activation after exactly one BMC reset without platform-health regression.
original_method: PATCH the source UpdateService apply-time property, POST each FPGA image to the source update URI, wait for completion, then query FirmwareInventory and inspect system logs.
manual_activity: An authorized engineer must define the destructive transition/reset contract and approve the image, host state, security and recovery plan before any agent-controlled write.
required_inputs: FPGA component/current/upgrade/downgrade versions, order and signed image hashes
Vendor-advertised Redfish action, payload, task and apply-time contract
Definition of the sole BMC reset and activation evidence
Approved secret/TLS handling and recovery path
safety_requirements: Do not execute the embedded URL credential or TLS-bypass commands.
Do not infer `/UpdateService/update`, Immediate apply or a TaskService monitor without target capability evidence.
Never retry, reverse direction or add a reset after an uncertain write.
Keep stable power and independent BMC/FPGA/host recovery available; preserve raw failure evidence.
agent_execution_scope: After the conflict is resolved, perform capability discovery and one approved API transition at a time, poll only the advertised task and collect version, reset and health evidence.
Do not issue a firmware write while the reset and host-state semantics remain unresolved; do not set the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve host state, transition order, reset initiator/count/timing and activation criteria.
Approve images, vendor Redfish contract, security/recovery plan and final verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Redfish lifecycle is relevant, but the source hard-codes a credential, disables TLS verification and assumes an update URI; DeepSeek also contradicts the source by requiring the host powered off.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No write command is authorized. After resolution, discover the target-advertised UpdateService action and use a credential-redacted, trusted-TLS, vendor-approved client flow.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The booted-host wording, supplied PATCH/POST/GET, 10/30-minute values and one-reset criterion remain verbatim evidence.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING DETERMINISTIC REDFISH FPGA UPDATE CONTRACT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve the source conflicts, bind immutable images to the advertised component/action, capture a task or synchronous terminal response, account for the one approved BMC reset and independently verify active FPGA plus host/BMC health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the named BMC/FPGA combination after capability and vendor-procedure confirmation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Redfish service/schema, BMC firmware, FPGA component/image and client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Target vendor Redfish FPGA update, activation and recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Would replace embedded secrets, TLS bypass and assumed endpoints with discovered and approved contracts while retaining both direction tests.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Adds unambiguous reset accounting, active-component evidence and independent platform-health checks.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner decision on host state and one-reset semantics plus vendor contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A generic Redfish UpdateService contract does not prove vendor FPGA support; no endpoint or payload may be invented.

project_override_considerations: A project may select images, versions, order and vendor action only after resolving the source-level host-state and reset ambiguity. Completion is limited to the approved transition plan.
expected_evidence: Approved conflict resolution and immutable transition matrix
Capability/action discovery and redacted request/response transcript
Image signatures/hashes and task terminal state
Pre/post active FPGA inventory and exact reset timeline
Host POST/OS, BMC health and SEL evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items/Procedure require the system booted, while the same-row DeepSeek risk says host powered off; the criterion also requires only one BMC reset without defining initiator, timing or whether each direction receives one reset. These facts change destructive execution.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Unlike ordinary missing project inputs, the required operating state and acceptance reset semantics are mutually unclear. A safe firmware state machine cannot be executed without an owner decision.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its unsafe credential/TLS and powered-off substitution while retaining its API potential.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees that the present destructive contract is blocked, with V3.1 making clear that images and versions alone would only be readiness inputs.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates genuine semantic conflict from ordinary project parameters and preserves automation capability for later reassessment.

review_improvement: Pinpoints the two execution-changing ambiguities and prevents an assumed generic Redfish endpoint or hidden reset from becoming evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: The software core could become fully automatable, but today the source requires an undefined single-reset acceptance while its same-row guidance disagrees on host state. Because either interpretation changes firmware safety and activation, this is an irreducible source conflict rather than a package gap.
